claims.text: Illness can interrupt attendance at school and work, add caring time and absorb household income. Malaria is caused by a parasite transmitted through bites of infected mosquitoes; it is not caused by drinking dirty water. Safe water, sanitation and hygiene instead reduce exposure to infections associated with faecal contamination, including cholera. Mosquito control and reducing bites address a different transmission route. Match prevention to the route rather than presenting one measure as protection against all diseases. Immunisation uses vaccines to develop protection against particular infections; it is not treatment for every existing illness. Programmes need trained personnel, dependable supplies, suitable storage and reachable services. This is a development explanation, not personal diagnosis or a vaccination schedule.

claims.text: Percentage change compares a change with the starting value. Subtract the old value from the new value, divide that difference by the old value, then multiply by 100. If attendance rises from 80 to 100 users, the increase is 20 users; 20 divided by 80 is 0.25, giving 25% growth. If it falls from 100 to 80, the change is −20 users; dividing by the original 100 gives −0.2, or a 20% fall. The different denominators explain the different percentages. Percentage points instead subtract two percentages, such as coverage rising from 40% to 55%, a gain of 15 points. Starting from zero makes this percentage-change division undefined; report the absolute change.
